business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business section (P1) and reiterated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4)
business_model.claim: CF Industries' core product is anhydrous ammonia (NH3, 82% nitrogen, 18% hydrogen), which it sells directly or upgrades into nitrogen fertilizer and industrial products; its principal customers are cooperatives, retailers, independent fertilizer distributors, traders, wholesalers and industrial users.
quotes: Our core product is anhydrous ammonia (ammonia), which contains 82% nitrogen and 18% hydrogen.
Our principal customers are cooperatives, retailers, independent fertilizer distributors, traders, wholesalers and industrial users.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A sales-volume table (P3)
business_model.claim: The company reports five product segments: Ammonia, Granular Urea, UAN, AN, and Other (primarily DEF, urea liquor, nitric acid and aqua ammonia).
quotes: (1)Other segment products primarily include DEF, urea liquor, nitric acid and aqua ammonia.

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by two multiplicative factors: the global commodity selling price per ton and the number of product tons shipped; in 2025 the average selling price rose 19% to $372/ton and volume rose 1% to 19.1 million tons, together lifting net sales to $7,084 million (table in millions).
quotes: The average selling price for our products was $372 per ton in 2025 compared to $313 per ton in 2024.
We shipped 19.1 million tons of product in 2025 compared to 18.9 million tons in 2024.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3) and the 8-K earnings release sensitivity table (P5)
business_model.claim: Natural gas is the largest and most volatile component of manufacturing cost, representing approximately 34% of production costs in 2025 (28% in 2024), because it serves as both chemical feedstock and fuel in the Haber-Bosch process.
quotes: Natural gas is the largest and most volatile component of the manufacturing cost for our nitrogen products, representing approximately 34% and 28%, respectively, of our production costs in 2025 and 2024.

business_model.claim: The business is seasonal: the strongest North American demand occurs during the spring planting season, with a second peak following the fall harvest, so the company builds inventory during low-demand periods.
quotes: The strongest demand for our products in North America occurs during the spring planting season, with a second period of strong demand following the fall harvest.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Business and MD&A sections (P1, P3) and the 10-Q MD&A (P4)
business_model.claim: The company is decarbonising its ammonia network to create a differentiated low-carbon product for new applications (power generation, steel production in Japan) and to help European customers offset carbon border adjustment costs; the Donaldsonville CCS project (completed July 2025, ~$200 million) enables up to ~1.9 million tons of low-carbon ammonia annually.
quotes: Our low-carbon products are expected to be used for existing and new applications, such as power generation and steel production in Japan, and to help customers reduce the economic impact of European regulations on the price of carbon.
In July 2025, construction, commissioning and start-up of the dehydration and compression unit at our Donaldsonville complex was completed for a total cost of approximately $200 million.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K (P1, P3), the 10-Q MD&A (P4) and the Q3 2026 earnings release (P5)
business_model.claim: The Blue Point One joint venture (CF 40%, JERA 35%, Mitsui 25%) is a ~$3.7 billion greenfield ATR ammonia plant with CCS at Modeste, Louisiana; construction commenced in August 2026 and low-carbon ammonia production is expected to begin in 2029, with a nameplate capacity of ~1.4 million metric tons (~1.5 million tons) per year.
quotes: We estimate that the cost of the low-carbon ATR ammonia production facility with CCS technologies will be approximately $3.7 billion.
State and federal permits were received in July 2026, enabling construction at the Blue Point complex to commence in August 2026.

Natural gas is the largest and most volatile component of the manufacturing cost for our nitrogen products, representing approximately 34% and 28%, respectively, of our production costs in 2025 and 2024.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Trade policy uncertainty, including the U.S. Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling that IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs and the subsequent imposition of a 10% tariff on most imports, creates uncertainty that may impact the cost of capital equipment for CF's Blue Point project and global nitrogen trade flows.
quotes: On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that IEEPA does not authorize the president to impose tariffs, including IEEPA-based global tariffs and tariffs on imports from Canada.

The Supreme Court decision did not modify non-IEEPA tariffs, including tariffs on imports of certain steel and aluminum products and their derivatives which may impact the cost of our capital equipment, including for development and construction at our Blue Point complex.
